r: **Mashelkar Committee → National Auto Fuel Policy (2003) → Euro norms**
**Euro-based norms under the Bharat Stage name from 2000** (four-wheelers); BS-I was also called **"India 2000"**
**1992**; India generally lagged Europe by about **5 years**
Tailpipe standards under the **Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989** by **MoRTH**; CPCB/MoEFCC set the pollution side (CPCB under MoEFCC also credited with implementation)
**No sale or registration of BS-III (and below) vehicles from 1 April 2017**
**No sale or registration of BS-IV vehicles from 1 April 2020**
BS-IV straight to BS-VI – urgent **Delhi-NCR** air pollution; closes the gap with Europe in **one step**; BS-V is the only stage skipped
BS-IV and BS-VI are based on **Euro 4 and Euro 6**
**RDE introduced for the first time**; **On-Board Diagnostics (OBD) is mandatory**
Refineries had to supply **10 ppm fuel nationwide**; sulphur cut 500 → 10 ppm in about **15 years**
Euro / BS norms limit **CO, hydrocarbons, NOx, PM**; Euro norms also cover **lead**
NOx **60 mg/km petrol, 80 mg/km diesel**; diesel PM **4.5 mg/km**
Diesel NOx → N₂ + water using urea **AdBlue**
Respiratory illness; forms ground-level ozone and acid rain
Reaches deep lungs/bloodstream; heart and lung disease
Needs NOx + hydrocarbons + **sunlight** (cannot form without sunlight)
Pollute water, soil and the food chain
Mandatory under the **CMV Rules, 1989** – generally **6** months; **12** months for BS-IV/BS-VI vehicles
Notified **17 Feb 2026**; all States/UTs from **1 April 2026**, minimum **RON 95**; replaced the **2021** E10 notification
Cars from **April 2027**; credits for ethanol, CBG, biofuels; targets about **21% relaxed** vs the Sept **2025** proposal
Automated Testing Stations + **Registered Vehicle Scrapping Facilities**
